details: For every finite nonempty binary class and fixed known admissible distribution $\mu$, deterministic adaptive proper queries identify the target in expected cost at most $\log_2|\mathcal H|$, counting all queries and requiring no final confirmation once the target is known.
witness_verification: For the $n$ singletons and the empty concept, $\log_2|\mathcal H|=\log_2(n+1)$, whereas proper random-counterexample query complexity is one for every admissible $\mu$, by proposing the empty concept (value404). The first parameter divided by one plus the second tends to infinity.
name: Log Size / Random Proper Equivalence Queries Complexity
proof_source: Survey Theorem thm:random-proper-query-log-size gives the weighted closest-to-mean proof including acceptance and singleton cases. Angluin--Dohrn, The Power of Random Counterexamples, Theorem 21, establishes the same numerical upper bound using Max-Min.
